ai.description: This 50–70 cm viper is bright green with a yellow-white lateral stripe. It is distinguished by its exceptionally large, heavily keeled dorsal scales and a dark-bordered, triangular head.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Trimeresurus macrolepis* is best distinguished by its exceptionally large, heavily keeled, and overlapping scales that give it a distinct, rough-textured appearance.
ai.habitat: The Large-scaled Pit Viper inhabits high-altitude evergreen forests and shola grasslands in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 1,200 and 2,400 meters.
ai.behavior: The Large-scaled Pit Viper is primarily nocturnal, often remaining motionless among foliage to ambush passing frogs and small mammals with a rapid, precise strike.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Trimeresurus macrolepis* is viviparous, typically producing a litter of 5–12 young. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, primarily between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Large-scaled Pit Viper is endemic to the high-elevation evergreen forests of the Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically occurring above 1,500 meters.
